newsitem.title: UK: Northern Foods affected by commodity prices.
newsitem.headline: Northern Foods affected by commodity prices.

text.p: Sir Christopher Haskins, chairman of British food producer Northern Foods Plc, said the company's dairy business continues to be affected by the decline in commodity prices.

"The dairy business continues to be affected by the decline of commodity markets compared with a period of exceptionally high prices last year," said Haskins. Northern reported a one percent increase in its profits before tax and exceptional items of 57.8 million pounds ($96.82 million) for the six months ended September 30.

The company's dairy business posted operating profits of 21.6 million pounds, down 27 percent, reflecting a sharp deterioration in dairy commodity prices. Competition in the supermarket sector also remains intense, with some erosion of prices in recent months, said Northern.
However, the company said the decline in the doorstep delivery of milk, which averaged nine percent across the business in the first half, was better than it expected.

Northern's prepared foods division, which supplies foods like the Pork Farms Bowyers meat products and a range of convenience foods, reported a 24 percent increase in trading profits to 43.1 million pounds.

The improvement was achieved despite consumers concern over a link between mad-cow disease and a similar brain wasting disease in humans which hit sales of convenience foods and meat pies. Northern estimates the beef crisis cost it about 3.0 million pounds in the first half. ($1=.5970 Pound)
